partner_context.their_ambition: Movia is the public-transport authority for Greater Copenhagen, and it runs the harbour buses — the yellow Havnebus lines that cross the harbour as ordinary public transport. Since a 2020 contract, those harbour buses have run fully electric. Movia's ambition is a completely fossil-free, zero-emission network, on the water and on land, inside a city targeting carbon neutrality.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric upgrade to a harbour bus network Movia already runs fully electric. The Nyhavn–Opera–Refsaleøen run and the new harbour-district stops — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and still zero-emission, on the same Rejsekort ticket, from the harbour-bus stops that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Copenhagen, Denmark · Movia (Greater Copenhagen public transport)
hero.title: Navier × Copenhagen Harbour Buses — the harbour, on foils
hero.subtitle: A foiling-electric layer on Movia's already-electric harbour buses — Nyhavn, the Opera, Refshaleøen and the new harbour districts: faster and just as clean across a harbour Copenhagen already crosses on electric ferries.
hero.what_we_do_together: Movia brings the harbour bus network, the stops and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same harbour — faster and still zero-emission — extending the electric harbour bus Copenhagen already runs.

why_now: Copenhagen's harbour buses have run fully electric since 2020 under Movia's contract, inside a city with one of the world's most ambitious carbon-neutrality goals. The network is already clean; a foiling-electric fleet is how it also gets fast — turning harbour crossings into quick, low-wake links as the city keeps building new waterfront districts like Refshaleøen and Nordhavn.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the Movia network at Nyhavn, where the harbour buses meet the metro and the city. A single Rejsekort carries a passenger from the metro straight onto a foil to the Opera, Refshaleøen or the new harbour districts — the existing electric harbour buses keep the frequent short hops underneath.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: Copenhagen's harbour buses are already fully electric.
proof_points.evidence: Since Movia's 2020 harbour-bus contract, the Havnebus lines have run on fully electric vessels.

proof_points.claim: The harbour buses are public transport, not tourism.
proof_points.evidence: The yellow Havnebus lines run on the ordinary public-transport ticket as scheduled harbour crossings.
Copenhagen has one of the world's most ambitious municipal carbon-neutrality programmes.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: The harbour buses are already electric — why change?
objections.response: Because foiling adds speed and range the current displacement vessels can't reach — turning slow harbour hops into quick links as the city keeps building new waterfront districts, while staying zero-emission.

objections.concern: Will it disturb a dense, built-up harbour?
objections.response: No — low wake and near-silent operation are gentler on the harbour edge and its houseboats and swimmers than conventional hulls.

objections.concern: Does this replace the harbour buses people rely on?
objections.response: No — the existing electric harbour buses keep the frequent short hops; foiling adds a faster layer to the longer and growing runs.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first Movia harbour link — most likely the growing Nyhavn–Refshaleøen run — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the Rejsekort ticket.

close.body: Copenhagen already runs its harbour buses on electricity. Navier is how they also get fast — a quick, near-silent, low-wake crossing to the Opera, Refshaleøen and the new harbour districts, on the same public ticket, and just as clean.
